title: opum-sdlc: disarm auto-merge when a PR's content reopens for discussion
summary: Candidate rule for opum-sdlc, from opum-agent, to fold into whatever opum-workflow release comes next -- filed for the record now, not to be started before then. Not urgent, but the incident that prompted it is real: lore-cli armed auto-merge on a multi-select PR, a design question then reopened what that PR should contain, and while the discussion ran CI went green and auto-merge landed the superseded behaviour on dev -- the exact default the discussion had just concluded was wrong. Caught only because a follow-up push reported 'create a pull request' instead of updating the existing one, since the branch was already deleted on merge. THE RULE: do not leave auto-merge armed on a pull request whose content is under discussion; disarm it when the question reopens, not when you remember the PR exists. Auto-merge is a decision made in the past that executes in the future -- correct for settled content (tracker chores, mechanical syncs, fixes with no open question), wrong the instant the content is live again, because the merge then happens on CI's schedule rather than anyone's judgement. Worth pairing the rule with why the blast radius stayed small: the wrong default reached dev and never reached main, because promotion is a separate deliberate act -- that is the fast-forward discipline working as designed, and a rule that only says 'do not do this' teaches less than one that also says why dev is where a mistake is cheap.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Add the rule to opum-sdlc's SKILL.md as prose the fleet will actually read at the point auto-merge is armed, not just a changelog line -- the incident was caused by relying on memory ('remember to check the PR'), so the fix must not itself rely on someone remembering to look for it.

Place it where the reader is already thinking about auto-merge: the existing 'What is automated' section's allow_auto_merge bullet ("a PR lands itself once checks go green") describes the exact mechanism this rule caveats, and is a more precise, findable location than the Deliver section opum-agent proposed as a starting guess, which describes landing chores generally but never mentions auto-merge specifically. Placement is this task's call to make, not a rubber-stamp of the first suggestion.

Include the contained-blast-radius reasoning (dev absorbs the mistake because promotion to main is a separate deliberate fast-forward act) alongside the prohibition, not just the prohibition alone -- the incident write-up shows that pairing teaches more than the rule by itself.

Land this in the same release that carries OMARK-23's already-stacked fix (both ride opum-workflow's CHANGELOG Unreleased section per the current release hold, dated to close 2026-09-15) rather than as a separate standalone version bump.

implementationNotes: Filed at opum-agent's (orchestrator) request, 2026-09-09. Not to be started now -- explicitly 'nothing to do now', captured for the record so it survives until the next deliberate opum-workflow release.

lore-cli is independently recording the same incident on its own task, so it survives there too if this release slips or if opum-sdlc's own edit lands from a different repo's session than this one. Reconcile the two records rather than duplicating the fix when this is picked up -- check lore-cli's tracker for its own task id before starting.

This is a skills/ change, so it will trip the same 'check . manifests' content-changed-means-version-moved guard OMARK-23's fix did -- add (or extend) an Unreleased CHANGELOG.md entry rather than bumping plugin.json's version, for the same reason OMARK-23 did: a mid-window release would force another fleet restart and reset OMARK-21's observation baseline.
